# dsh-plugin-hub
**One control hub for every plugin and skill installed in DeepSeek Harness (dsh).**

DeepSeek Harness ships a deliberately barebones core — "everything is a plugin".
Within weeks its co

mmunity produced turn rewind, long-term memory, skill cards,
failure-experience libraries, Obsidian

bridges, browser automation, local
transcription, security scanners... and then you face the real pr

s, browser automation, local
transcription, security scanners... and then you face the real problem:

> You have 7 plugins across profile bundles, a skills directory, and built-in
> tools. You can't rem

ember which one does what, whether it's actually running,
> or what you installed last week.
`dsh-plugin-hub` is the missing front door:

- **One routing table** (`SKILL.md`) — the agent answers "which tool for X" from a
single, maintaine

d table instead of guessing across plugin lists.
- **One status command** (`status.ps1`) — profile p

lugins, tool files, services,
and skill junctions, checked in one shot.
- **One install step** (`ins

tall.ps1`) — copies the hub and junctions it into
`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\skills` so DSH hot-loads it. S

kills stay in one unified
directory; no more copy-pasting folders into `.dsh`.
- **One manifest** (`

PROVENANCE.md`) — what you installed, from where, which
license, verified how. The routing table is

only allowed to claim what this
file confirms.
- **Safety rules baked in** — third-party skills are

untrusted by default; scan
before install; no safety-policy-bypassing or account-pool plugins.
## Two ways to run it

**1. As a dsh bundle (recommended).** The repo is an installable DeepSeek
Harness bundle: `package.j

son` declares `dsh.bundle`, and `cordis.patch.yml`
registers the plugin. Installing it adds three to

bundle`, and `cordis.patch.yml`
registers the plugin. Installing it adds three tools to the session:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Tool | Answers |
| `hub_plugins` | what is installed in this profile, which version, and whether each bundle is actua

lly present on disk |
| `hub_check` | PASS/WARN/FAIL per check — profile manifest, third-party bundl

es on disk, skills directory, local services — each with a fix hint |
| `hub_route` | "which plugin
handles X", from a maintained routing table, including whether that plugin is installed |

All three are read-only: nothing is installed, removed or patched. Platform
bundles (`@deepseek-ai/*

`) are reported as `BUILTIN` — they ship inside the
harness, so a missing `node_modules` copy is nor

s `BUILTIN` — they ship inside the
harness, so a missing `node_modules` copy is normal, not a fault.

The npm name is `dsh-control-hub` (`dsh-plugin-hub` was already taken on npm);
the GitHub repo keeps

h-control-hub` (`dsh-plugin-hub` was already taken on npm);
the GitHub repo keeps the original name.

**2. As a skill + CLI scripts.** The original layout still works and needs no
Node: `install.ps1` co

pies the hub skill and junctions it into
`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\skills`; `status.ps1` / `doctor.ps1` /
`gen-provenance.ps1` run outside the harness. See Quick start below.

## Health checks

`status.ps1` gives you the inventory; `doctor.ps1` gives you a verdict per check
with a fix hint, an

d `-Fix` applies the safe repairs (UTF-8 BOM, missing
junction):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That WARN is the point: a loaded plugin is not a running service, and the hub
says so instead of let
ting a call fake-succeed.
## Compatibility
| dsh version | Status |

| 0.2.0-rc.2 (Desktop) | tested — hub in production use |
| 0.2.1-rc.2 (Desktop) | tested — incl. tu

rn-rewind 0.3.10 compat fixes |
| 0.2.1-rc.3 (CLI `headless`) | tested — bundle installs, activates,
and a real session's model calls `hub_check` and reports its values |
Windows-first (junctions, PowerShell). PRs for other platforms welcome.
## What it does NOT do

- It is not a plugin manager (`dsh plugin add/remove` still does that) — it is
the discovery, dispat

ch, and truth-keeping layer above your plugins.
- It does not collect or send anything anywhere. All

paths come from your local
`config.ps1`, which is git-ignored.
## Roadmap
- [x] Installable bundle: `dsh.bundle` + `cordis.patch.yml` contributing `hub_plugins`, `hub_check`,

`hub_route` (read-only)
- [x] 30-second demo GIF (`docs/demo.gif` — rendered from a sandbox run by

`docs/make-demo-gif.py`; profile prefix shown as `C:\Users\you`)
- [x] `doctor` mode: per-check PASS

/WARN/FAIL with fix hints (`doctor.ps1`, `-Fix` applies safe repairs)
- [x] Provenance generator: au

to-draft the manifest from `dsh plugin list` (`gen-provenance.ps1`, `-Online` enriches via npm)
- [
] Community routing-table presets (security, media, office workflows)

t): see the studio page

his pattern? Open an issue or reach out — this repo grew
